utterances.text: We have provided a copy of that to the Defence and have an additional copy, if necessary, for the Court. (To the witness): While you were in the camp at Omarska, did you see any of the Muslim men who had been community leaders in Prijedor in that camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While there do you recall seeing Braco Ceric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw Ceric called "Braco". He was the President of the Court. I saw Mohamed Cehajic, Professor, who was the Mayor of the municipality of Prijedor. I saw Idriz Jakupovic who was the head of the Red Cross. I saw Professor Crnkic, Professor Puskar, Professor Hadzalic, Professor Mujagic, Dr. Eso Sadikovic. I saw many policemen, all businessmen, Dedo Crnalic, Asaf Kapetanovic, Sead Ramadanovic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Ma'am, when you saw these leaders in the camp, did you see any signs of beatings or injuries or wounds to these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What types of injuries did you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were open wounds. One of the doctors had his arm broken. Idriz Jakupovic had his arm broken. Professor Husein Trnkic who taught mathematics had his clavicle, his collar bone, broken and also had injuries on the wound. Ado Ekimovic and his father hardly had a clear spot on their faces. So that one could see their faces and they were all people of distinction.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Ma'am, do you know a man named Dule or Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you happen to know him or know of him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I learnt about him because my relatives were in his karate club.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did they ever point him out to you or only speak about him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they pointed him out to me.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long before the war, how many years before the war, had you known Dule Tadic, Dusko Tadic? How many years before the war had you known Dule or Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About three or four years.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How would you characterise your knowledge of him? Would you say you were friends, that you recognised him when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Acquaintances only.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During these years that you knew him before the war, how many times would you say in total you had seen him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 20 times or thereabouts maybe.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where would you see him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kozarac, in the street, walking, in Prijedor I also saw him.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Before the attacks began in opstina Prijedor when you saw Dusko Tadic, did you ever see him with a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When was the last time you saw him before your arrest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometime in the middle of June in Prijedor at the marketplace.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you saw him on this occasion, did he have a beard or was he clean shaven?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Clean shaven.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In June '92 at the marketplace he was clean shaven?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know what his occupation was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he had a coffee bar.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was there anything unusual about the way he walked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, since he knew how to put his chest forward and then he walked like this, from one side to the other.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You mean he walked side to side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am going to move to another matter. This might be an appropriate time to break?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess for 20 minutes. (4.00 p.m.) (Adjourned for a short time) (4.20 p.m.) (In the absence of the witness)

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is a matter that I would wish to go into with this witness that raises a question of law that needs to be determined before I would pursue that line of questioning. So I would raise that now so that the Defence would have an opportunity to object, if they choose to. In the direct examination, the witness had indicated that she saw Dusko Tadic in June 92 at the marketplace in Prijedor and that at that time he was clean shaven. In a statement ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You did not like that answer.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, ma'am, I must be honest. In a statement she had given us previously she had indicated that at that time when she saw him he had a beard. It would be my intention to ask her if she recalled giving that statement, if she recalled saying in that statement that he had a beard and then to ask her which is correct, whether he was clean shaven or had a beard.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. The issue here is an interesting one, as I know jurisdictions vary in their approach to this matter. What the Prosecution would be seeking to do is cross-examine their own witness on the previous statement. Miss Hollis was good enough to raise this matter with me during the short adjournment and provided me with a copy of the statement this time. My submission to the Court is that this is really a province for cross-examination by me if I choose it, and seeking to impeach her own witness in this fashion is not something that we would support.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. I believe that, as Defence counsel noted, this issue is decided differently in different jurisdictions. I know for some years many years ago in my jurisdiction and in the federal jurisdiction, I believe, in the United States you could not do that. It has been sometime now that we are allowed to do that, to ask them about prior statements that are inconsistent with their testimony. I am certainly not treating her as a hostile witness, but I would agree that in the sense of the word that we normally talk about impeaching a witness, in a sense I would be doing that by asking her these questions. I would suggest, in the light of the other conversations we have had in this courtroom about approaches taken to evidence, that would be an appropriate thing to do. I know, however, as I say, there are different approaches taken so I wanted to raise it with the Defence and give them the opportunity to object.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: As far as Mr. Kay, your suggestion that this is a matter for cross-examination and for you to decide whether you want to raise it or not on cross-examination; I suppose, as a tactical matter, the party offering the witness at least should be given the opportunity to decide how they want to approach it. In other words, it is Miss Hollis's problem and to say it may not be a problem because of how you might handle it on cross-examination really I do not think solves the problem. The real problem is whether or not in our Tribunal the witness, under certain circumstances, should be subject to either impeachment or however you want to call it, cross-examination, in the face of this. There are many approaches. Let me confer with my Judges and see. Perhaps the witness can be asked if she recalls making a statement and then whether or not this statement refreshes her memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: But you are right, it would be an impeachment of the witness because there is no indication that her memory needs refreshing at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If I could just raise one matter, your Honour? I do not think that this is a witness that would have reached hostility and shown animus as against the Prosecution in relation to her evidence.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: We agree with that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: As far as I am concerned, this little bit, whether it was a beard and whether she said at one point that he had a beard and now she is saying, no, that he was clean shaven, perhaps in the scheme of things it is not going to be tremendously important, but then I do not know because I do not know where you are and where you are coming. So let us see a moment. (The learned Judges conferred)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We have determined that we will allow Miss Hollis to question the witness -- I do not want to use the word "impeach" nor do I want to use the word "cross-examination" -- but bring to the attention of the witness the fact that she had given this statement prior to her testimony today and in the statement she then said that he had a beard. Is that right or is it the other way around ---

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: -- had a beard. So that you will be able to do that. That being done, again we will consider the fact that Miss Hollis has had to do this as affecting the weight that should be given to the testimony. In other words, if she says on direct he was clean shaven and now, with the benefit of the statement, the witness says that she at the time saw him with a beard, then the question in our mind is what weight should we give to her testimony regarding the condition of Mr. Tadic's face, whether it was clean shaven or a beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am grateful for the Court's indication on that matter.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. Would you ask the witness then to come forward?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. HASIBA HARAMBASIC, recalled.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, you may resume.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. (To the witness): Ma'am, if I could return to a matter we were discussing just prior to the break? Prior to the break you had testified that when you saw Dusko Tadic in June 1992 in the marketplace in Prijedor at that time he was clean shaven. Do you recall giving a statement to representatives of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In that statement do you recall discussing the time in June 1992 when you saw Dusko Tadic in the marketplace?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In that statement do you recall indicating that at that time in June 1992 in the marketplace Mr. Tadic had a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As I indicated, on direct you have stated that he was clean shaven. Could you please tell the Court what is your recollection? On that date in June 1992, was Mr. Tadic clean shaven or, to your recollection, did he have a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a beard.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. During the time that you were in the Omarska camp did you ever see Dusko Tadic in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How many times did you see him there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Twice.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When was the first time that you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About mid July.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where were you at the time that you saw him in mid July?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you saw Mr. Tadic at that time what was he doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was walking across the pista.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At the time that you saw him did you have a full face view of him, a profile view or both?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Both, because he turned towards the pista and towards the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How far away would Dusko Tadic have been from you on that occasion when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About three or four metres.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At that time what was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Blue jeans.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At that time did you see any weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he had a pistol attached to his blue jeans.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you saw him on that occasion was there anyone walking with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: For how long a period of time did you see him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A couple of minutes, the time it took him to cross the pista.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On that occasion when you saw him, did Dusko Tadic have any facial hair or was he clean shaven?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a beard.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What time of the day or night was this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 1 o'clock in the afternoon, half past one, roughly.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So it was during the day time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the day time.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At the time that you saw him was there anything obstructing your view of him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When was the second time that you saw him at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The second time I saw him was on 23rd July 1992.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Are you able to give a specific date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had a calendar on my person and I used to cross the days that had gone by and that day, I circled that day on my calendar.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did the circle signify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The circle signified the date that was particularly meaningful to me.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On this date, on 23rd July, when you saw him, where were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in the dining room.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where was Dusko Tadic when you first saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was at the second window. He came by car and stopped next to the second window, on the upper side of the dining room.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did you see after he drove up in a vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He came out of the vehicle and another gentleman, the other gentleman. They both walked along the road and then Dusko Tadic stopped with a guard called Joja on the pista and the other gentleman went on towards the path leading to the white house.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did you see then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After a couple of minutes of conversation with a heavily built young man, blond, who was wearing glasses, it was a specific dress in a special way, he had a t-shirt with multi-coloured sleeves and the lower part of a camouflage uniform, green, and at the back he had a patch, a brown. When he parted with him, he went on to the path leading to the white house.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You say he went on to the path leading to the white house, who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am referring to Dusko Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did you see then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then the inmates started coming out. The first one to come out was Dr. Jusuf Pasic; the second one to come out was an engineer, Nasic; the third one was Zlatan Besirevic who had his hands behind his head; the fourth one was Seljanovic Rufat and the fifth was Enes Begic; the sixth, Agos Zardikovic; the seventh was Crnalic Armin called "Caruga" and then two gentlemen I do not know from that group. Then they walked across the pista. There was Dr. Osman Mahmuljin and Ziko Mahmuljin.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These men that you have just mentioned, you mentioned a Dr. Besic, who is Dr. Besic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dr. Begic, Enis, was a surgeon in the health centre in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was there a Dr. Besic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there is no Besic, it is Begic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These people that you mentioned did you know them from before the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you know them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you know them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were my good friends. Dr. Osman was my very good friend. Dr. Ziko Mahmuljin was a good friend. Dr. Begic, Enis, the surgeon, was a very good friend of mine because we were born in the same place. Dr. Seljanovic, Rufat, worked with me across from my office in the surgery, and I knew engineer Zlatan Besirevic, I had known him very well. He was a family friend. I also knew Armin Crnalic called "Caruga" because he was the owner of a restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the ethnic group of all these men that you have just named?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you saw them moving from various directions across the pista, in what direction did they then move?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They went on across the pista towards the red house.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: From the position where you were sitting in the restaurant building, were you able to see all of the way down to this red house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not all of the way, part of the way from the intersection towards the white house, down along that way for about 50 metres I could see.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What happened after you saw these men moving toward the red house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After about 10 minutes they were followed by Mr. Dule Tadic and the gentleman who accompanied him. After a couple of minutes two guards followed them, two guards followed them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After you saw all of these people going toward the red house, did you see Dusko Tadic again that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him coming back from the red house. I followed him with my eyes. He came to a car, got into the car and left.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You have indicated that when you first saw Dusko Tadic on that day you saw him at the second window on the side of the restaurant building, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Are you talking about the side of the restaurant building that is facing toward the Judges?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you saw him at that time, how far away do you think he was from your position in the restaurant building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About five or six metres.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Five or six metres from where you were to the second window in the restaurant building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As he walked along that building to the area on the pista where he stopped, did you have a full face view of him, a profile view or both?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When he stopped on the pista and spoke with this person, Joja, how far away do you think Dusko Tadic was from where you were sitting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Three or four metres.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At that time did you have a full face view, a profile view or both?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As he walked to the white house and stood at the white house, did you have any view of his face at all, either a profile view or a full face view?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see him, I saw his face.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You saw his face as he stood by the entry sidewalk to the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During this entire incident this day, how long in total would you say that you saw Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe 15 or 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On this date what was Dusko Tadic wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On this date did he have any weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a short automatic gun.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your recollection, on this date was he clean shaven or did he have a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a beard.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you left Omarska camp did all of the women in the camp come with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How many women were left at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Five women were left in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did two of those women eventually come out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, after two weeks after us Sabija Turkanovic came out, then Zdenka Rajkovic and Mugbila Besirevic, Hajra Hadzic and Velida Mahmuljin remained behind.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Would you please at this time look around this courtroom and see if you recognise the man you know as Dusko Tadic in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Would you please look at him and point to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where he is sitting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the back row, in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask you to note a proper identification of the accused?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, the record will so reflect.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please be seated, Mrs. Harambasic. When you left Ormaska, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Into a second camp in Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you were in Trnopolje did you see the Commander of the camp there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Slobodan Kuruzovic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know him from before the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he used to be the principal of the elementary school, Sesnaesti Maj. His wife used to work with me as a dental assistant.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is his ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where did you go from Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Home.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Back to your home in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long did you remain in your home in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two months.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What were the conditions like for you during those two months that you were in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Horrible. We were not allowed to go out. We were not allowed to lock our doors. We could not buy anything to eat. They kept calling us on the telephone all night. Everybody, all sorts of people came into the house. They seized our car, things. There was abuse, very bad abuse, all the time.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How were you eventually able to leave Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had to leave Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How were you able to do this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I found a gentleman by the name Rajko Maric, because I could not obtain my papers in the regular way, I paid him two and a half thousand German marks and he gave me two, two ID cards in Serbian names. Then he took me in his car with another gentleman, who is an inspector, a SUP inspector, from Prijedor to Banja Luka. From Banja Luka they put me on a bus and I set out towards Vojnic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you have to pay any additional ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In addition to the two and a half thousand German marks, I gave 500 marks to Rajko so that he could pay at checkpoints, so that I could be let through the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Prior to the events in opstina Prijedor and the attacks in opstina Prijedor, were you a member of any anti-Serb military or paramilitary organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you a member of any organised anti-Serb resistance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After the beginning of these attacks did you become a member of any such organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Cross-examination, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You say that you knew Dusko Tadic before the conflict and had seen him some 20 times perhaps. What I would like to know is over what period of time you say that you knew him, for how long?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About five or six years.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had you ever spoken to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Have you ever sat down at a table with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The way that you say you came to know him was because relatives of yours had had training at his karate school, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The relatives that you say had this training with him, did they live in Kozarac or Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Am I right in thinking that you lived in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had cousins since, not only in Prijedor, but also in Kozarac, in Banja Luka, in all the towns, in all the Bosnian towns.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I was actually asking where you lived. Did you live in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When your relatives spoke to you, did they say, "We have karate lessons with a man called Dusko Tadic"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But, presumably, they were not with you when you saw him on all those 20 occasions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were very often.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But that is not every time, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not every time but very often.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On those occasions when you were with your relatives, they did not speak to Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So the way that this person was pointed out to you was, presumably, in circumstances of passing in the street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In those circumstances, presumably, that person was of no particular interest to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you say you saw the man Dusko Tadic on those occasions over six years, can you describe what he looked like before the conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a strong man, normal height -- what else can I say?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you could tell us whether he had a beard or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he did not have a beard when I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember the last time you would have seen him before the conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What date would that have been, what time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember perhaps how long before the conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On that occasion when you saw him was he clean shaven?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did he have a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he had a small beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you say you saw him after the conflict in Omarska and in the marketplace in Prijedor, your evidence has been that he was with a beard although you have said he was clean shaven?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I said he had a beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Earlier this afternoon in fact you said he was clean shaven.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, we have this recorded which was why ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I made a mistake because of the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, it was not the translation. It was the words that you said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: OK.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you speak English at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It was the words that you said, that he was clean shaven then, and I wanted to ask you why, that you had said that and then in another statement said he had a beard.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I made a mistake. He did have a beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just looking then at the description of the man you say was Dusko Tadic before the conflict, did he have no beard during that period of time, or did he have a beard sometimes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did not have a beard. I never saw him with a beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So the man you saw after the conflict was looking differently from the man you had seen before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but you can recognise a man by his eyes, by his manner of walking, by height, by the general appearance and not just by whether he has a beard or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On that occasion that you said that he had a beard after the conflict, was it a beard that also had a moustache?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, in the statement you have been referred to by Miss Hollis this afternoon reminding you that actually you said he had a beard and was not clean shaven, you also said he had a moustache. Perhaps you would like to look at it. The passage is here marked in ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, I would not look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, I am sorry, I am going to have to ask that you do. This would be tendering D22, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is this the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is the statement Miss Hollis had earlier in the Serbo-Croat.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you would just read to yourself that passage which has the purple mark beside it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. "While I was in the camp a man called Dusko Tadic came to the camp. I had known him before the camp. He was the owner of a coffee bar and a karate expert. He was about 1.85 metres tall or 1.88 with black hair. When I saw him in Omarska he had a beard and a moustache." You asked me just now when I saw him in the marketplace in Prijedor whether he had a beard, a moustache then. You did not ask me whether he a moustache in Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You are able to make that distinction then, are you, between seeing him in Prijedor in the marketplace and seeing him in Omarska ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- with a moustache or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With a moustache, with a small moustache.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you can describe for us the length of the beard that you saw him wearing on those occasions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To begin with I am not a man and I do not know how a beard grows. It was a short beard. It was not a beard in the conventional sense of the word. I mean, it was not like this and I do not know how it grows. I am not a man.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you would like to give us an indication of the length of the hair, how many centimetres? You are holding up your fingers. I do not know whether the Court saw that as a representation?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Will you hold your fingers up again, please, Dr. Harambasic? That is an inch and a half. You will convert it to centimetres, will you not?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is not --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two and a half, two, three centimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In those six years that you say you would have seen this man over 20 occasions, were they in particular periods of one time or were they spread over the six years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I should say spread over that period, often, whenever I came to Kozarac I saw him and I often came to Kozarac. It could have been more times than 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The clothes that the man was wearing in Omarska on the two occasions that you saw him, can you tell us what clothes they were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first time he had jeans and a dark blue shirt, that is a t-shirt, and had a pistol in his trousers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The second time ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And the second time he had a camouflage uniform, I already said that, and in his hand he had a short automatic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was the camouflage uniform wearing a jacket or was it a shirt that was worn on the top?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was a camouflage t-shirt and camouflage trousers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So the t-shirt then was without long sleeves? Was it short sleeves?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No jacket on the top?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The second time you saw him then on this occasion that you have told us is 23rd July, can you remember if he had a weapon with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a short automatic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that a short automatic rifle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How was that being carried?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So not being put over the shoulder or carried on the back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, down in his hand and he had it backwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You see what I suggest to you, ma'am, is this, that in fact you are mistaken when you say that the man you saw in Omarska on those occasions was Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, I am not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What I would like to put to you is this. Do you know a man called Miso Danicic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Nothing on redirect, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Madam, do you know a person by the name of Fikret Harambasic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Additional questions, Miss Hollis, or Mr. Kay. Miss Hollis first?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There is one matter that Mr. Orie has pointed out to me that I should put to the witness, your Honour. (To the witness): In that statement that I have handed to you, madam, on the next page you say that the both times you saw Tadic he wore a camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I repeat it again, the first time he had a pair of jeans on, black jeans, a dark blue blouse and he had a pistol at the back of his trousers. The second time he was in a camouflage uniform, a camouflage shirt and he had a short automatic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What I am concerned with is your accuracy of recollection of these matters and ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember it very well because I was in Omarska, not you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you explain then how when you came to recollect these matters in February 1995 that you said something different?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That you said that he wore a camouflage uniform on both occasions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you think in fact that your memory is at fault about these matters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, my memory serves me well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Nothing, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection to Dr. Harambasic being permanently excused, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Dr. Harambasic, you are permanently excused. You are free to leave. Thank you for coming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, would you call your next witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would ask the Court's indulgence for a very short break. Our next witness is a person who has some emotional difficulties in waiting. I would like to make sure that the witness is emotionally prepared to come into the courtroom. Things may go more smoothly if I am allowed a very short time for that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: How much time do you need?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Just five minutes. If I could perhaps leave the courtroom for that time?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It is acceptable?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour, for that indulgence. Your Honour, at this time the Prosecution would call Suada Ramic. MRS. SUADA RAMIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Would you please stand and take the oath. Would you please take the oath? Mr. Usher, would you give the oath and ask the witness to please read that oath. Would you read that oath, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In translation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Would you please state your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Suada Ramic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 4th February 1955.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you born in the town of Prijedor or in a village in the opstina of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Donja Cela in the municipality of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is your marital status?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Married.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is your husband's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Adem Mehmedovic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is your ethnic group or nationality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is your husband's ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You lived in Donja Cela until when?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometime between 1980 and 1982.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where did you move to at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the municipality of Prijedor, to Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How many people lived in this village of Donja Cela?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a small hamlet.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the ethnic group of the inhabitants?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were Muslims mostly.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How far was Donja Cela from the town of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 3.5 to 4 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know people in villages surrounding Donja Cela?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge what was the ethnic group of people in those villages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Predominantly Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long did you live in the town of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, since 1982 until 1992.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Until when in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until about June, until we went to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was your occupation a driver and conductor for Auto Transport Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long did you work for Auto Transport Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From 1978 to 1992, until 1992.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know a man by the name of Dule or Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In passing.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You knew this man to recognise him when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In 1991 did you perform duties as a Reserve Police driver and drive to areas that were within a few kilometres of the confrontation lines with Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Based on your observations there did you at some point refuse to continue to perform those duties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when I saw what they were doing. Of course not only I, most of us.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was your refusal to continue to perform those duties known by people in the town of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, about most of them, not only about me, but most of them, they knew that we had refused because it was not, that it was injustice, that it was destruction of a people.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: A few days after the Serb takeover of the town of Prijedor, did you go to your brother's home in Donja Cela?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On the way back from that visit were you stopped at a checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know any of the people who stopped you at that checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the ethnic group of the people who stopped you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sometime after that were you taken to the Prijedor police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you interrogated there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know the person or people who interrogated you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How do you know them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, in passing because he often travelled with us, would come to the station of public security and he was the head of the shift.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was this person's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dragan Banovic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was his occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Police Commander.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was his ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After that interrogation did a man named Brkic take you to the military barracks in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Brkic an Auto Transport driver.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the name of the military barracks to which you were taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zarko Zgonjanin.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At sometime while you were at the military barracks were you blindfolded and taken to a room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What happened to you after you were blindfolded and put into that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took me to a dark room.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They raped me. They raped me and took me back for interrogation to the same corridor from which they had taken me away.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then after that what happened with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was bleeding heavily and the soldier who interrogated me in that room invited me to enter the room. When I entered the room, as I was covered in blood, he said simply: "What fool did that?" He gave me a blanket and asked me only where I lived and I told him Petra Preradovica 25, the first street off another street, and he drove me there. After that I called the hospital to see whether they could help me. I asked for Dr. Katzman or Dr. Banovic or nurse Liljia or Jalja or Vikica. Banovic answered my call and I told her what happened. I told her I started bleeding out of fear and she said: "I cannot help you like this. Come to the hospital." I went to the hospital. I took a taxi and when I came to the hospital she received me and only said: "First I have to see what is wrong with you", and when she examined me she told me I was pregnant, about three or four months, or something like that she said, and said: "Listen, I have to perform the abortion but I do not have the anaesthetic." She invited another doctor, Savic, and when he entered the room he started cursing and saying that all balija women, they should be removed away, eliminated, and he also started cursing her because she was helping Muslims and saying that all the Muslims should be annihilated, especially men. She gave me some pills and told me: "If anything goes wrong, further wrong, I cannot help you any more." I returned ----

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could stop you there for a moment. You indicated that a doctor there helped you. What was that doctor's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dr. Banovic, Mrs. Banovic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated another doctor that was cursing and saying things such as all balija women should be removed, what was that doctor's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dr. Savic, Mr. Savic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So while you were at the hospital they found it necessary to abort your pregnancy, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated that this was done without the benefit of any type of anaesthesia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then you were sent home from the hospital, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you reached home was your husband at your home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When had been the last time that you had seen your husband?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some 10 days before this happened.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Prior to the rape at the military barracks had you had any physical problems such as bleeding or cramping, any problems with your pregnancy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you got home to your apartment a few days after that, did you go to your brother's home in Donja Cela?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you arrived there had most of the women left the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were there do you recall men in uniforms coming to the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know these men who came to the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and those were neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What are the names of the men that you knew?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Momir Marinovic and Mico Dobrijevic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You said they were neighbours from a village close by?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, from the village, this one where we were born.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the ethnic group of these men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What orders or ultimatums did they give when they came to you in this village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The automatics, to turn over weapons and to put up white rags, white cloth on the windows, to mark them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were there any weapons in this village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only lawful ones, I mean, people who had licences to have weapons.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What type of weapons were these, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only pistols.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were these weapons turned in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you then go to find the women and bring them back to the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you pass through the village of Carakovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the condition of the homes in that village when you passed through?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Burned down and shelled.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you know, what ethnic group had lived in that village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were on this trip to find the women and bring them back, did you see any bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bodies, yes, I did see them, but I paid no attention because I was afraid.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you find the women and take them back to the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you then return to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.
